problem: Existing multi-task navigation foundation models (NavFoM, ABot-N0) bake in one fixed observation-context strategy (uniform sub-sampling or sliding window) that cannot be reconfigured at deployment, although instruction following, object search, tracking and driving need very different temporal context.
motivation: Agentic systems (e.g. long-horizon EQA) need a navigation executor whose task mode and context strategy an outer planner can change mid-episode. Different tasks need global history (VLN, exploration) versus recent frames (tracking, approach), and no single fixed strategy serves all.
key_idea: Build a Qwen3-VL-based waypoint-predicting navigation model with a parameterised interface (task modes plus token budget, temporal decay, camera weights, frame-sampling mode) trained under full randomisation so an external planner can reconfigure it at inference.
insight: Framing multi-task navigation as controllable observation-context modelling, with training-time randomisation over the parameters, gives one model usable across tasks and configurations with no architecture change. The token-budget/decay sweep shows the knobs matter: on 500 R2R val-unseen episodes, SR rises from 70.8 (B=2048) to 74.6 (B=4608), and larger gamma raises OSR from 78.8 to 82.6. Scaling data helps long-horizon tasks most, and co-training with VL data is claimed to prevent collapse into reactive mappers, but no ablation is reported for that claim.
method: Waypoint policy: Qwen3-VL backbone (SigLIP-2 ViT, DeepStack) plus a 4-layer MLP head (hidden 512, GELU) that outputs 8 waypoints (x,y,theta); MSE loss on normalised waypoints.

Task-adaptive token allocation: weight matrix W[t,c]=exp(gamma*t/(T'-1))*w_c; budget B (2048-4096) is spread proportionally with per-image floor b_min and ceiling b_max, iteratively clamped; each image is resized to its allocated token count.
Frame sample mode and randomisation: random (global coverage) vs latest (recency window), 50/50 in training; B, gamma, camera weights, b_min and b_max are randomised per sample.

Natural-language viewpoint/time tags and embodiment prompt: 'Time step t Front View <image>...' tags and 'you are a robot/car' preambles; no architecture change, and new embodiments need only a new prompt.

Co-training data: 15.6M samples: 85% trajectories (VLN-CE R2R/RxR 5.63M, PointNav 984K, ObjNav 2.0M skeleton-based, tracking 1.49M, driving ~3.2M, plus 40K text-to-video-derived), 15% VL/reasoning data; Qwen-Image-Edit photorealism, instruction paraphrasing, camera augmentation; L = L_traj + L_VL.

Agentic system: Qwen3.6-Plus planner decomposes goals and calls nav(sub-goal, task mode, config); a harness returns trajectory-evidence records, key frames and an evidence notebook (two-level memory), plus auxiliary vision tools.
Deployment: 4B model on Unitree Go2, cloud 196 ms vs Jetson Thor FP8/TensorRT 204 ms per step.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL 4B and 8B (fine-tuned end-to-end) + MLP action head; agentic system adds Qwen3.5/3.6-Plus planner (frozen)
setting.training_data: 15.6M samples: 85% navigation trajectories (R2R/RxR CE, PointNav, ObjNav, EVT-Bench tracking, nuScenes/OpenScene driving, 40K T2V-generated) + 15% VL/reasoning data (~1.0M general VL, 873K nav reasoning, 362K discrete multi-round nav)

results: QwenNav-8B reaches 72.1 SR on R2R-CE and 76.5 SR on RxR-CE (panoramic), beating NavFoM by 10.4 and 12.1 SR and the strongest baseline OmniNav (69.5 / 73.6). It also gets 90.0 TR on EVT-Bench and 91.4 PDMS on NAVSIM, and the agentic system sets a new SOTA on three EQA benchmarks (HM-EQA 76.7 vs FAST-EQA 69.2). It trails on EVT-Bench SR (78.6 vs ABot-N0's 86.9), on OVON SPL and on zero-shot AlpaSim.
limitations: Lower SR than tracking specialists on EVT-Bench, lower SPL on OVON due to exhaustive skeleton-style exploration, and far behind Alpamayo-R1 on zero-shot AlpaSim.
The token allocation is an admitted heuristic; ObjNav is compared to baselines evaluated on HM3D v1 versus v2, and the benefit of VL co-training is asserted without an ablation.
The agentic EQA system depends on a proprietary large planner (Qwen3.6-Plus), and real-robot results are qualitative only.
